name: Generic Quake 1 engine
summary: The command line every id-derived Quake engine documents, for an engine this build has no profile for.
description:
This profile makes no claim about any particular engine. It sends only the four switches id Software's own Quake documented and every derivative kept: `-basedir`, `-game`, `+map` and `+connect`. Use it to get something running, then say which engine it actually is — a real profile knows what its engine supports, and this one cannot.

It declares no `host_dedicated` action, because whether a given build has a dedicated server compiled in is exactly the kind of thing a generic profile does not know.

This profile was written from Generic Quake 1 engine's own published command-line documentation, not from a build running on this machine. That is what every `unverified` platform below means, and it is why there is no version probe: asking a Quake engine what version it is means starting it, and starting it means opening a window and a game.

`play_map` names a game directory as well as a map, because that is what these engines' command lines do: `-game` chooses which directory the map is loaded from. Launching a map into a directory nobody named is how you end up watching the wrong map.

license.name: Not asserted — the licence is whatever your engine's is
license.notice: Quake engine source ports are separate programs under their own licences. This profile configures one; it does not contain, link or relicense it. Game data — PAK files, maps, textures and sounds shipped with a commercial release — is not covered by that licence, and the Companion never copies, uploads or redistributes it.
